title: NeuralMesh: Neural Network For FEM Mesh Generation in 2.5D/3D Chiplet Thermal Simulation
problem: 3D chiplet packaging with dense Through-Silicon Via (TSV) arrays requires fine FEM meshes for accurate thermal simulation, but traditional iterative mesh refinement is computationally expensive.
motivation: Chiplet-based IC systems demand high-fidelity thermal analysis, but existing FEM mesh generation methods lack scalability for intricate 3D/2.5D geometries with dense interconnects.
method: A neural network predicts how heat will spread through the chip based on its shape, materials, and power consumption. Instead of iteratively refining the mesh (repeatedly tweaking the computational grid to get better results), the network's predictions directly optimize an initial rough mesh. The network identifies thermal hotspots where detail is needed and automatically reduces mesh detail in cooler regions, cutting computation while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: A neural network generates thermally accurate meshes directly from heat predictions, eliminating iterative refinement and achieving 45× speedup while staying within 0.8% of COMSOL accuracy.
contributions: Enhanced segmentation model predicting thermal distributions from design parameters
Direct mesh optimization guided by learned thermal predictions, eliminating iterative refinement
45× mesh generation speedup while maintaining 0.8% thermal accuracy vs. commercial COMSOL
Adaptive coarsening reduces mesh elements in non-critical regions
primary_theme: Neural-network-guided mesh generation for rapid chiplet thermal simulation
